name: Execute public market trades
summary: A four-person trading desk executes the orders that internal equity, fixed income and credit portfolio managers, pool cash deployments and total portfolio overlays release to it. A trader accepts each order, chooses between a broker algorithm, a negotiated block, a program trade for baskets, competing dealer quotes for bonds and currency, or a new issue or auction order, and watches it until filled, carried over or cancelled. Fills are checked against broker summaries and allocated across pools and client accounts the same day so trade support can match them, and overnight cost analysis flags expensive orders. Delays come from large orders worked over hours or days, quotes outside limits and fill discrepancies; errors come from manual allocation and voice fills.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian provincial public-sector asset manager with about 240 staff and a small internal desk trading equities, government bonds, credit, currency and futures for pools and client accounts.
baseline.notes: The internal desk is assumed in the organisation file once strategies were internalised; the model manager does not describe it publicly.

trigger: A compliance-checked order from a portfolio manager, a pool cash deployment, an overlay adjustment or a newly approved counterparty's first order appears on the desk blotter.
end_state: The order is filled or its residual cancelled, the allocated trade ticket has gone to trade support and the next-day cost review is closed; or the order is withdrawn or cancelled.

volume.seasonality: Peaks at month end, index review effective dates and large pool flows; heavy in market stress such as March 2020.

evidence.note: Organisation file demand driver: about 900 internal public market orders a month, program trades counted per security.

steps.name: Order arrives on the trading blotter
steps.description: An order released by a public equity, fixed income or credit portfolio manager, a pool cash deployment basket or a total portfolio overlay order appears on the desk's blotter in the order management system with the originator's instructions, already through pre-trade compliance.

evidence.note: Orders begin in the portfolio or order management system and pass compliance before the desk.

steps.name: Accept the order and check its instructions
steps.description: A trader picks up the order, checks the security, side, size against average daily volume or market depth, limit and urgency, whether the market is open, and that the brokers or dealers it may go to are approved with room under their counterparty limits, then accepts it.

error.defect_description: An unusual instruction or ineligible counterparty is not noticed.

control.basis: Approved broker and counterparty list: brokers pass due diligence before handling assets (OSC exemption order condition) and counterparty limits are loaded from counterparty onboarding

next.condition: instruction unclear or order hard to trade

evidence.note: Query rate is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Query the order with the portfolio manager
steps.description: The trader messages or calls the portfolio manager to explain the issue (limit away from the market, size large against volume, halted security, news) and suggests a wider limit, longer horizon or smaller size, then waits for the amended or confirmed order.

evidence.note: Portfolio managers and traders agree the strategy together.

steps.name: Choose the execution method and counterparties
steps.description: The trader decides how to execute: a broker algorithm or direct market access for routine equity and futures orders, a negotiated block with a broker's sales trader for large or illiquid names, a program trade for a rebalancing basket, requests for quotes to several dealers for bonds and currency, or an order into a new issue or auction. Very large or sensitive orders need the head of trading's agreement.

evidence.note: U.S. institutional equity volume was 44% high touch and 35% algorithmic or DMA in 2021; order shares here are the author's estimate for a desk with large bond and program flows.

steps.name: Head of trading agrees the strategy for a large order
steps.description: The head of trading reviews the pre-trade cost estimate, the order's share of daily volume and the risk of information leakage, and agrees the broker shortlist, horizon and whether to seek a block or a risk price.

control.basis: Trade management policy: senior sign-off on execution strategy above size or liquidity thresholds

evidence.note: Author estimate of desk practice.

steps.name: Route the order to a broker algorithm
steps.description: The trader picks an approved broker and algorithm (VWAP, implementation shortfall, percent of volume, target close or a dark aggregator), sets the limit, participation rate and start and end times in the execution system and sends it electronically.

error.defect_description: Wrong algorithm parameter or limit entered.

control.basis: Approved broker list and best execution policy

steps.name: Negotiate a block with a broker's sales trader
steps.description: The trader calls or chats with an approved broker on a recorded line, describes the order without revealing more than needed, asks for natural block interest or a capital commitment, agrees the commission and hands over the order.

control.basis: Approved broker list, recorded lines and conflict policies (front running, soft dollars) under the OSC exemption order

steps.name: Bid the basket as a program trade
steps.description: For a pool deployment or rebalancing basket the trader sends anonymised basket characteristics to three or four program desks, compares their agency or risk bids, awards the basket and agrees the benchmark, usually the close. The work is shared across every order in the basket, so time per order is small.

control.basis: Best execution policy: competitive bids for program trades

evidence.note: Liquidity-driven trades typically use closing prices; bid process is the author's description.

steps.name: Program desk executes the basket
steps.description: A risk bid is filled at once at the agreed price; an agency program is worked by the broker through the day to the benchmark, often the close, and fills for each security come back to the execution system.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Broker or algorithm works the order
steps.description: The algorithm or broker slices the order into many child orders across exchanges and dark pools according to the chosen strategy until it completes, reaches its end time or hits its limit; fills stream back to the execution system.

evidence.note: Average algorithmic parent order runs 84 minutes; the mode is set higher because pension orders are larger and many target the close.

steps.name: Request quotes from dealers and execute the best
steps.description: For bonds, money market instruments, currency forwards and swaps the trader sends a request for quotes to three to five approved dealers on a multi-dealer platform or by chat, compares the prices, executes with the best and keeps the losing quotes as best execution evidence; if no quote is within the limit the trader goes back to the portfolio manager.

error.defect_description: Wrong value date, settlement terms or quantity agreed with the dealer.

control.basis: Best execution policy requiring competing quotes for over-the-counter trades; FX Global Code principle on fair and transparent order handling

evidence.note: Share without acceptable quote is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Return to the portfolio manager when no quote is acceptable
steps.description: The trader tells the portfolio manager the best levels available; the manager accepts, changes the bond or size, or cancels, and the trader asks for quotes again or closes the order.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Place the new issue order or auction bid
steps.description: The trader places the portfolio manager's order with the syndicate desk of a new issue, or the bid through a government securities distributor for an auction, before the book or bidding closes, then waits for the allocation, which is often smaller than the order.

evidence.note: Author estimate; primary allocations are made by the syndicate or the central bank auction.

steps.name: Monitor the working order and adjust
steps.description: While the order works the trader watches fills against arrival price and interval VWAP, changes participation or limits when prices move, pauses for news or halts, and switches broker if performance is poor.

steps.name: Decide on the unfilled residual
steps.description: At the end time or the close the trader checks the unfilled quantity, consults the portfolio manager on a material residual, and either carries it to the next session with a handover note or cancels it as a partial fill.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Escalate unusual conditions to the head of trading
steps.description: The trader brings the head of trading an order that is moving the price, a broker outage or a news event; the head decides whether to continue, change broker or strategy, or stop and consult the portfolio manager.

next.condition: stop and decide on the residual

evidence.note: Written trade policies set escalation procedures.

steps.name: Order waits for the next trading session
steps.description: The order management system rolls the carried order to the next session as a good-till-cancelled order; over a weekend or holiday the wait is longer.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Check fills against the broker's execution summary
steps.description: When the order is done the trader compares the fills in the execution system with the broker's or dealer's end-of-day summary (quantity, average price, commission) and keys any voice fills that did not arrive electronically.

control.basis: SOC 1 control objective: trades authorised and recorded accurately, completely and timely

evidence.note: The model manager obtained a SOC 1 Type I report in 2021; rates are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Resolve a fill discrepancy with the broker
steps.description: The trader asks the broker's desk to correct or cancel the wrong fill, checks the corrected execution report and notes the fix.

next.condition: turns out to be a trade error

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Handle a trade error
steps.description: The head of trading confirms the error, decides the correcting trade, makes sure the pool or client account is made whole and the cost borne by whoever caused it, informs the portfolio manager and compliance and logs the incident.

control.basis: Trade error policy (SOC 1 control area: trade errors and guideline breaches); client made whole

steps.name: Allocate the execution across pools and client accounts
steps.description: The trader confirms the allocation of the block across pools and client accounts in the order management system, using the portfolio manager's pre-allocation and pro rata shares for partial fills at the average price, so trade support can confirm with the broker on trade date.

error.defect_description: Allocation to the wrong account or not pro rata.

control.basis: Fair allocation of investment opportunities among members and pools (OSC exemption order condition); FX Global Code principle 47 on allocating block transactions promptly

evidence.note: About 80% of institutional allocations happen after the close on trade date.

steps.name: Release the trade ticket to trade support
steps.description: The order management system sends the allocated trade ticket with price, quantity, broker, commission and settlement details to trade support and the matching service for confirmation with the broker before the matching deadline.

control.basis: NI 24-101: institutional trades matched as soon as practical and by noon on T+1

steps.name: Record the best execution rationale
steps.description: The trader notes in the execution system why the broker, dealer or venue was chosen, the competing quotes or bids received and any block or risk price, so the decision can be reviewed later.

control.basis: Trade policy record keeping for best execution; books and records condition of the OSC exemption order

steps.name: Overnight transaction cost analysis screens the order
steps.description: Overnight the transaction cost analysis service compares the order's prices with arrival price, interval VWAP and the close and flags orders whose cost falls outside set limits for their size and difficulty.

evidence.note: Outlier share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Explain the cost outlier
steps.description: The trader opens the order's timeline of fills, market moves and news and writes a short explanation of why costs were high (news, thin liquidity, poor broker or algorithm performance, late start).

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Head of trading reviews outliers and broker performance
steps.description: At the weekly review the head of trading goes through outliers and explanations, decides whether broker or algorithm choices should change and keeps notes for the periodic best execution report.

control.basis: Best execution monitoring under the trade policy

evidence.note: All trades should be evaluated for execution quality and broker performance.

exceptions.name: Order queried with the portfolio manager
exceptions.description: The trader cannot work the order as instructed and agrees a change with the portfolio manager, who sometimes withdraws it.

exceptions.name: Unfilled residual carried over
exceptions.description: A large or illiquid order is not complete at the close and is carried to the next session.

exceptions.name: No acceptable dealer quote
exceptions.description: Bond or currency quotes are outside the limit; the portfolio manager adjusts or cancels.

exceptions.name: Fill discrepancy
exceptions.description: The broker summary differs from the fills recorded; the broker corrects it.

exceptions.name: Trade error
exceptions.description: A wrong side, quantity, security or account is traded; the head of trading corrects it and logs the incident.

exceptions.name: Cost outlier review
exceptions.description: Overnight cost analysis flags the order; the trader explains it and the head of trading reviews it weekly.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the order reaching the blotter to the close of the next-day cost screen

evidence.note: Most orders complete the day they arrive (average algorithmic parent order 84 minutes) and are allocated after the close on trade date; the overnight cost screen adds about 16 hours; p90 covers orders carried over and outlier reviews.

benchmarks.unit: share of volume, year to Q1 2021
share of trades by value and volume to be matched by noon on T+1 before an exception report is required
benchmarks.population: Canadian registered dealers and advisers under NI 24-101

pain_points.description: Three traders cover equities, bonds, currency and futures across time zones, so orders queue at the open, at month end and on index dates.

evidence.note: Organisation file: trading desk of four.

pain_points.description: Bond and currency trades are priced by chat or platform quotes and some fills arrive by voice, so they are keyed by hand and checked against broker summaries.
Allocation across pools and several client accounts happens after the close under a matching deadline, inviting misallocations.
Large or illiquid orders run over several sessions, delaying the portfolio managers' intended positions.

sources.title: The model manager 2021 Annual Report
sources.supports: Read as the text copy saved under scratch/. Three equity pools and the public market alternatives pool ($29.2 billion pooled at end 2021); pooling brings operational efficiencies in day-to-day pool activities and cash management; public equities combine internal fundamental, factor (size, quality, value, momentum) and index strategies with external managers; fixed income ($17.2 billion) is managed internally for capital preservation and liquidity against FTSE Canada government indices; global credit ($6.0 billion) does not separate public and private credit, plans to internalise through direct co-investments, invested US$500 million with Antares (sponsor-backed middle-market direct lending) and US$500 million with Ares; PMA uses a managed account platform with 12 managers; Investment Policy Statements per strategy set permitted investments and restrictions; Management Investment Committee and three Investment Department Committees (Total Portfolio, Equities and Credit, Real Assets) approve up to thresholds; clean SOC 1 Type I report at 30 September 2021.

sources.title: The model manager, Commission and Director decisions (exemption order)
sources.supports: Read as the text copy saved under scratch/. The model manager exempted from adviser registration on conditions; Board-approved policies must cover a compliance system, books and records, conflicts including front running, soft dollars and fairness in allocating investment opportunities among members and pools, prevention of investments that contravene restrictions set out in each investment management agreement, due diligence on sub-advisers, and due diligence on custodians and brokers before they hold or access assets.

sources.title: Asset Manager's Guide to SOC 1
sources.publisher: SIFMA Asset Management Group and Grant Thornton
sources.supports: Read as the text copy saved under scratch/. Baseline SOC 1 control objectives: trades properly authorised, settled and recorded in accordance with portfolio guidelines and account restrictions; contributions and distributions authorised by the client and processed accurately; other control areas include brokerage allocation (best execution, soft dollars, IPO and new issue allocation), broker selection and retention, trade aggregation, trade allocation, trade errors and guideline breaches.

sources.title: Accelerating the U.S. Securities Settlement Cycle to T+1
sources.supports: Read as the text copy saved under scratch/. Settlement cycle of trade date plus two days (T+2) in the period; about 20% of institutional allocations occur during the trading day and 80% after the close on trade date; confirmation and affirmation can only start once allocations are complete.

sources.title: Trade Strategy and Execution (refresher reading)
sources.supports: Order, security, market and portfolio manager inputs (size against daily volume, liquidity, volatility, urgency) drive trade strategy; algorithm classes are scheduled, liquidity seeking, arrival price, dark aggregators and smart order routers; equities trade largely electronically except very large or illiquid trades, fixed income bilaterally through dealers, currencies OTC; index and liquidity-driven trades use the close; arrival price, VWAP and close benchmarks; implementation shortfall is the standard cost measure; a written trade policy covers best execution, trade errors, eligible brokers and venues and execution monitoring, and all trades should be evaluated with transaction cost analysis.

sources.title: The Anatomy of Trading Algorithms
sources.publisher: Tyler Beason and Sunil Wahal, Arizona State University (NBER conference paper)
sources.supports: Read as the text copy saved under scratch/. 2.3 million algorithmic parent orders from 961 institutions; the average parent order tries to trade US$287,000 over 84 minutes, 4.8% of volume over its duration, and generates hundreds of child orders; VWAP, TWAP, implementation shortfall, target close and percent of volume algorithms are standard broker offerings.

sources.title: FX Global Code (updated December 2024; first published 2017)
sources.supports: Read as the text copy saved under scratch/. Principle 9: handle orders fairly and with transparency; Principle 17: disclosure of last look; Principle 47: review, affirm and allocate block transactions as soon as practicable, with each underlying counterparty approved.

sources.title: CSA Notice and Request for Comment: Proposed Amendments to NI 24-101 Institutional Trade Matching and Settlement
sources.supports: Read as the text copy saved under scratch/. Dealers and advisers trading for institutional investors must have policies to match trades as soon as practical and by noon on T+1 in the period; firms below 90% matched by the deadline must file a quarterly exception report (moratorium from July 2020); proposal to move the deadline to 9 p.m. on trade date for T+1.

sources.title: How Leading Buy-Side Trading Desks Are Rethinking Execution Management
sources.supports: Orders begin in portfolio or order management systems and pass compliance checks before the desk; fills and execution details flow back to the OMS for downstream processes; desks automate routine orders under rules they set and keep larger, less liquid or opaque orders high touch; broker selection is a trader judgement; TCA compares outcomes across brokers and venues.

sources.title: High-Touch Equity Trading Declines
sources.supports: High-touch trading fell to 44% of U.S. institutional equity volume in the year to Q1 2021 from 56% in 2012; algorithmic, DMA and smart order routing rose to 35% from 29%.

assumptions: The model manager has not described its trading desk; the organisation file assumes one of a head of trading and three traders. Practices follow industry guidance and a peer desk design.
Order sources follow the process map: about 58% equity, 30% fixed income and credit, 6% pool deployment baskets and 5.5% overlays; a newly approved counterparty starts only a handful of first trades.
Execution method shares (40% algorithm, 16% program, 32% request for quotes, 5% new issue or auction, 4% negotiated block, 3% large orders needing the head of trading) are author estimates.
Trade capture, confirmation and settlement belong to trade support; this workflow ends at the trade ticket and the next-day cost screen.
Time spent watching markets and talking to brokers outside individual orders is in the traders' stated full-time equivalents but not in per-order touch times.
Loaded costs per hour come from the organisation file.
